record.original_question: Does there exist a Siegel polynomial f_lambda(z) = lambda z + z^2, with theta irrational and f_lambda analytically conjugate to a rotation near 0, whose Siegel disk has boundary that is not a Jordan curve?

evidence.quote: Let fλ(z) = λz + z 2 where λ = exp(2πiθ). Call such a polynomial parabolic if θ is rational. If θ is irrational, and fλ is analytically conjugate to a rotation near 0 we say fλ is a Siegel polynomial.
Question 7. Are there any Siegel polynomials whose Siegel disk has a boundary which is not a Jordan curve?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For $\lambda = e^{2\pi i \theta}$ with $\theta \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z + z^2.$$
Suppose that $f_\lambda$ is analytically conjugate to the rigid rotation $z \mapsto \lambda z$ in some neighborhood of the fixed point $0$; that is, there exists an analytic conjugacy $\varphi$ defined on a neighborhood $U$ of $0$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, $\varphi'(0)\neq 0$, satisfying $\varphi(f_\lambda(z)) = \lambda\,\varphi(z)$ on $U$. The Siegel disk $\Delta_\lambda$ of $f_\lambda$ is the maximal such linearization domain containing $0$; it is a simply connected open subset of $\mathbb{C}$ on which $f_\lambda$ is conjugate to an irrational rotation. Such a polynomial $f_\lambda$ is called a Siegel polynomial.

Question: Does there exist an irrational $\theta$ for which $f_\lambda$ is a Siegel polynomial and the boundary $\partial \Delta_\lambda$ of its Siegel disk is not a Jordan curve?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open in general. Strong partial results are known: Petersen–Zakeri (Acta Math. 2004) proved that for almost every irrational rotation number the boundary of the Siegel disk of $\lambda z + z^2$ is a Jordan curve; bounded-type rotation numbers give quasicircle boundaries (Douady–Ghys–Herman–Shishikura); and Yang (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2016/preprint 1608.04106) showed the same for sufficiently high-type rotation numbers. No example of a quadratic Siegel polynomial with non-Jordan Siegel-disk boundary is known, and no proof covering all irrational $\theta$ is known.

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks with smooth boundaries (Buff–Chéritat), Acta Math. 193 (2004)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of quadratic Siegel disks with C^infty boundary; related to existence of Jordan-curve boundaries.
status_evidence.claim: Major progress on the structure of boundaries of quadratic Siegel disks, but does not resolve the question for all irrational rotation numbers.

status_evidence.title: The high type quadratic Siegel disks are Jordan domains (Yang)
status_evidence.snippet: For sufficiently high-type irrational rotation numbers, the boundary of the Siegel disk of e^{2 pi i alpha} z + z^2 is a Jordan curve.
status_evidence.claim: Result covers high-type rotation numbers but leaves the general case open.

status_evidence.title: Petersen–Zakeri, Acta Math. 2004
status_evidence.snippet: For Lebesgue-a.e. irrational rotation number, the Siegel disk boundary of the quadratic polynomial is a Jordan curve passing through the critical point.
status_evidence.claim: Almost-every-rotation-number result; not all irrationals are covered.
